headline: SELKIRK COPPER FILES MINTO NI 43-101: 47.8MT AT 0.89% CU — 940MLb COPPER RESOURCE TRIPLES TONNAGE IN YUKON, FEASIBILITY STUDY BEGINS SEPTEMBER
snippet: Selkirk Copper Mines Inc. (TSXV: SCMI) filed September 14 an NI 43-101 technical report for its Minto Copper-Gold-Silver Project in Yukon totalling 47.8 million Measured and Indicated tonnes at 0.89% Cu, 0.34 g/t Au, and 3.2 g/t Ag — containing 940 million pounds of copper, 530,000 ounces of gold, and 4.97 million ounces of silver — representing a 280% increase in M&I tonnage versus the prior 2025 estimate. Phase 2 drilling is more than 90% complete and SRK Consulting has been engaged to commence a Feasibility Study by end of September, targeting a Final Investment Decision in mid-2027.

headline: GREAT WESTERN MINING 92.98% TUNGSTEN RECOVERY AT NEVADA DEFENDER — ERIEZ FLOTATION UPGRADES 0.35% TO 7.21% WO3 CONCENTRATE, Q4 MAIDEN RESOURCE ON TRACK
snippet: Great Western Mining Corporation PLC (AIM: GWMO / OTC: GWMOF) announced September 16 initial metallurgical results from bench-scale flotation test work at its Defender Tungsten Project in Nevada — Eriez Flotation Division (Pennsylvania) recovered 92.98% of tungsten into a rougher concentrate grading 7.21% WO₃ from a starting bulk sample of 0.35% WO₃, pulling just 4.55% of total mass in the process. Cleaner circuit optimisation tests are next; the maiden NI 43-101 resource estimate and 2026 drill programme remain fully funded and on schedule for Q4 2026 delivery.

headline: TOP-10 SILVER MINERS HOLD RECORD $4.8B NET CASH — COEUR PAYS FIRST DIVIDEND SINCE 1994 AS SUSTAINED $70/OZ SILVER WIPES OUT SECTOR DEBT
snippet: The ten largest silver-focused mining companies collectively hold approximately $4.8 billion in net cash as of Q2 2026 — more than double the ~$2.0 billion peak during the 2010–2011 silver rally — as silver averaging above $70 per ounce over the past several months eliminated the balance sheet debt that plagued the sector for a decade. Coeur Mining (NYSE: CDE) paid its first dividend since 1994 in Q2 2026; Bloomberg data compiled by analyst Tavi Costa frames the cash accumulation as a structural shift, with producers now positioned for capital returns and M&A rather than the dilutive equity raises that defined past silver cycles.

headline: ARGENTINA MINING EXPORTS SURGE 75% TO RECORD US$4.74B IN H1 2026 — LITHIUM SHIPMENTS UP 185%, FULL-YEAR TRACKING TOWARD US$9B
snippet: Argentina's mining exports hit a first-half record of US$4.74 billion in H1 2026 — a 75% year-on-year gain — with gold generating US$2.485 billion (63% of total) and lithium cementing its position as the second-largest commodity at US$1.1 billion, up 185% year-on-year on both higher prices and a 68.2% surge in export volumes. Argentina projects US$12.1 billion in lithium and US$20.6 billion in copper exports over the next decade under its RIGI investment incentive framework; full-year 2026 mining exports are tracking toward a US$9 billion record, making Argentina the fastest-growing major mining export nation by percentage.

headline: DLP RESOURCES RECEIVES ESPERANZA DRILL PERMITS — FIRST DIAMOND HOLES AT PERU COPPER-GOLD-MOLYBDENUM PORPHYRY COMMENCE SEPTEMBER 18
snippet: DLP Resources Inc. (TSXV: DLP) received drill permits September 16 for its Esperanza copper-gold-molybdenum porphyry project in southern Peru, with the first diamond drill holes commencing September 18 — the project's first systematic drill test in its history. Esperanza is situated in Peru's Arequipa region within one of the world's most prolific copper-molybdenum porphyry belts; Phase 1 will test the primary porphyry centre defined by geophysical anomalies and surface sampling over two years of field work.

headline: FASTMARKETS EUROPEAN BATTERY MATERIALS CONFERENCE OPENS IN BUDAPEST — LITHIUM STABILIZES AT RMB 150,000/T AS WESTERN RECYCLING GAP TAKES CENTRE STAGE
snippet: The Fastmarkets European Battery Raw Materials conference opened September 15 in Budapest, Hungary, drawing battery supply-chain executives for three days of panels covering lithium price recovery toward approximately RMB 150,000 per tonne — easing from a RMB 156,000 August peak though still subject to the data volatility following SMM's September 4 inventory methodology change — and the structural gap between EU battery recycling targets and economic reality at current lithium carbonate prices. Mainstream forecasts presented at the conference point to a tight physical supply balance through 2026–2027, supporting a price floor irrespective of near-term data noise.

headline: GOLDSILVER.COM: SILVER'S POSITIONING TRAP POST-FOMC — 73RD-PERCENTILE SPEC LONGS FACE ASYMMETRIC RISK AS $64.98 CONFIRMS BUY-THE-NEWS
snippet: GoldSilver.com's pre-FOMC silver analysis — written with speculative net longs at the 73rd percentile of the past 60 weekly readings — mapped the asymmetric risk heading into Wednesday's decision: with the Fed delivering a well-anticipated 25-basis-point hike to 4.00% and guidance read as neutral rather than hawkish, silver responded with a buy-the-news move to $64.98 that validated the piece's base case. The analysis frames the 46.3-million-ounce annual structural deficit as the floor underneath any positioning unwind, with the $66.80 breakout level now the near-term technical target for a run at the year's highs.

headline: GOLDPRICEFORECAST: GOLD MAPS PATH TO $4,600 AFTER FOMC CLEARS — POST-HIKE SEASONALITY FAVOURS OCTOBER-NOVEMBER RALLY WINDOW
snippet: GoldPriceForecast's September 2026 analysis examines how the FOMC's 25-basis-point hike to 4.00% — the first since 2023 — clears the primary near-term headwind for gold, noting that in every well-anticipated tightening cycle since 2015, gold bottomed within six weeks of the first post-pause rate hike and proceeded into a multi-month rally. With gold rallying to $4,389 on the decision, Goldman Sachs holding a $4,900 year-end target and forward guidance non-committal on November, the analysis frames October–November as the highest-probability window for the next major leg higher.

headline: CAPSTONE COPPER PINTO VALLEY CEO INTERVIEW — ARIZONA MINE MODERNIZATION TARGETS LIFE EXTENSION AS U.S. COPPER DEMAND ACCELERATES
snippet: A Northern Miner CEO interview with Capstone Copper (TSX: CS) management at Pinto Valley in Arizona frames the operation's ongoing modernization as the key lever for extending mine life beyond the current schedule — targeting a 20% reduction in water usage per tonne of copper by 2026, a 6% improvement in ore recovery rates, and higher throughput to lift production guidance. Situated 130 kilometres east of Phoenix in the Globe-Miami district, Pinto Valley accounts for approximately one-quarter of Capstone's total copper output and sits in a jurisdiction increasingly prioritized by U.S. industrial policy seeking domestic copper supply.
